hints: Reflect the negative part of y=x+3a above the x-axis.
Mark the vertex (−3a,0), the y-intercept 3a, and two solid straight branches.
walkthrough:
Find key geometric features of $y = |x + 3a|$ with $a > 0$:
$$\text{Vertex on the } x\text{-axis where } x + 3a = 0 \implies x = -3a, \quad \text{giving vertex } (-3a, 0)$$
$$y\text{-intercept at } x = 0 \implies y = |0 + 3a| = 3a, \quad \text{giving point } (0, 3a)$$

Sketch the two linear rays forming a symmetric V-shape entirely on or above the $x$-axis:
$$\text{Right branch } (x \geqslant -3a): \quad y = x + 3a \text{ with gradient } +1$$
$$\text{Left branch } (x < -3a): \quad y = -(x + 3a) = -x - 3a \text{ with gradient } -1$$
$$\text{The graph is a V-shaped curve with sharp vertex at } (-3a, 0) \text{ and crossing the } y\text{-axis at } (0, 3a).$$

ai_rubric.Sketching Modulus Graphs: Sketches roughly symmetrical with vertex at $(-3a,0)$, $y$-intercept $3a$, two solid straight-line segments in both quadrants above the axis. Concludes that V-shaped graph with vertex $(-3a,0)$, crossing the $y$-axis at $(0,3a)$, with two solid straight-line branches above the $x$-axis.

hints: Compare y=|x+3a| with y=a−2x and find their genuine crossing from x+3a=a−2x.
Use the graph and a test point to choose where the V lies above the line; keep the boundary open and reject the extraneous squared crossing.
walkthrough:
Find the point of intersection between the graph $y = |x + 3a|$ and the straight line $y = a - 2x$:
$$\text{For the positive branch } x \geqslant -3a:$$
$$x + 3a = a - 2x$$
$$x + 2x = a - 3a$$
$$3x = -2a \implies x = -\dfrac{2a}{3}$$

Examine the other branch $-(x + 3a) = a - 2x$:
$$-x - 3a = a - 2x \implies x = 4a$$
$$\text{Check this intersection: at } x = 4a, \; |4a + 3a| = 7a \text{ whereas } a - 2(4a) = -7a.$$
$$\text{Since } 7a > -7a \text{ for all } a > 0, \text{ the line already lies below the graph here, so } x = -\dfrac{2a}{3} \text{ is the sole crossing point.}$$

Determine the region where $|x + 3a| > a - 2x$:
$$\text{Test } x = 0: \quad |0 + 3a| = 3a, \quad a - 2(0) = a.$$
$$\text{Since } 3a > a \text{ is true for all } a > 0, \text{ the inequality holds for all } x > -\dfrac{2a}{3}.$$

ai_rubric.Solving Inequalities: Derives critical value $-\dfrac{2a}{3}$ from $x+3a=a-2x$. Identifies Concludes with $x>-\dfrac{2a}{3}$. The final result is $x>-\dfrac{2a}{3}$.
